Title: Deterministic Layer-3 slice
Description: Reasoning-style retrieval with NO embedding/model dependency (tree/hierarchical retrieval over the L1 index; prior art REF-034 PageIndex). The embedding/AI dependency stays hard-gated; the LAYER does not. CANDIDATE FOUND 2026-08-10: Evokoa/pgGraph - a Postgres extension (Rust/pgrx, Apache-2.0) giving traversal/shortest-path/connected-components over EXISTING relational tables via a CSR index, with VERIFIED zero ML dependencies (full crate list is roaring/xxhash/bitvec/bincode/crc32fast/memmap2/serde). Additive to our tsvector index rather than a replacement, and it matches the ADR-0052 companion-artifact pattern. THREE ADR CAVEATS: (1) superuser=true trusted=false, so CREATE EXTENSION is installer-only, never the app role - check against enforced deployment profiles; (2) traversal functions do NOT enforce RLS, only table-level SELECT - VERIFIED 2026-08-10 and CONFIRMED by the project's own graph/src/acl.rs header and docs/known-issues.mdx. Mechanism: graph.build() compiles tables into an immutable memory-mapped CSR artifact and traversal walks that integer array, never the table access path, so RLS never runs; ACL is a preflight pg_class_aclcheck table gate, not a row filter. THE DECIDING FINDING is not RLS itself but that containment becomes CALLER-ASSERTED: 'hydrate' is a caller-supplied boolean and hydrate=>false skips the base-table query entirely, returning RLS-blind topology, while graph.weighted_shortest_path has NO hydrate parameter at all; 'tenant' is likewise caller-supplied and explicitly 'not verified against the calling role's identity'. Swapping a by-construction boundary for an argument-validation boundary is the exact regression our own war-room self-finding warns about. Tombstones compound it - under hydrate=>false a tombstoned node's coordinates stay reachable until sync/vacuum, breaking tombstone-as-governance-guarantee independently of RLS. Credits: build() FAILS CLOSED on RLS tables by default (graph.allow_rls_tables=off, PG021), no query function is SECURITY DEFINER so the traversal edge does not escalate, LEAKPROOF appears nowhere, and the docs are extensively explicit rather than silent. VERDICT: adoptable behind an ADR for OPERATOR-PLANE ANALYTICS ONLY - never on the agent-facing memory read path, and never granting EXECUTE on traversal functions to an agent-facing role; (3) prebuilt binaries DO exist - CORRECTED 2026-08-10: attested GHCR images for PG14-18 on amd64+arm64 remove the from-source pgrx build cost, but there is NO documented air-gapped install path, so we would mirror GHCR ourselves. Also confirmed: pgrx 0.19.1 / Rust 1.96 pin, superuser=true + trusted=false (a new superuser-installed C extension inside the same Postgres that holds the audit chain - its own blast-radius conversation), and the zero-ML crate list holds with two additions to our record (thiserror, serde_json). RULED OUT: semble (model2vec is a non-optional core dep), stash (requires BOTH an embedding model and a reasoning LLM), TencentDB-Agent-Memory (SQLite+sqlite-vec, no Postgres path, mandatory LLM endpoint).

SEQUENCING: removal must be the LAST fragment change, in the same ticket that stamps the frozen fragment, codegen drift zero. SHIPPED AS: PUT /v1/resources/{id} removed at T-131 from the fragment, the generated chi-server stub, the generated TS client, the handler (UpdateResource), and the store (Update) - codegen drift zero (byte-identical on re-run). Title: Containment - the enforced tool-execution boundary
Description: Adopt a sandbox so 'the gateway is the sole tool-execution path' becomes an ENFORCED property rather than an architectural assumption. Today our seven controls hold only if the agent chooses to call us, and nothing structurally compels that; worse, our one tool is remote.exec, so once an approved command runs on the target host that process's own network activity is entirely ungoverned. OWASP ASI02/ASI03/ASI05. LEAD PAIR (agent-verified 2026-08-10): matchlock (MIT; Firecracker microVM; programs nftables ITSELF via netlink in pkg/net/nftables.go so egress-through-proxy is a deployment property not a runbook step; synchronous allow/block/mutate hook over a Unix socket in pkg/policy/network_callback.go; Import(io.Reader) gives an air-gapped image path) PAIRED WITH iron-proxy (Apache-2.0; grpc transform to an arbitrary endpoint returning TRANSFORM_ACTION_REJECT, fail-closed on timeout; MCP tool allowlists with argument constraints that also filter tools/list so denied tools never appear to the agent). RISKS: matchlock is single-maintainer (497 of ~516 commits), 6 months old, self-labeled experimental, its hooks cover HTTP/HTTPS only (raw TCP is passed through uninspected) and its .deb does not bundle a guest kernel. RULED OUT: bromure (macOS/Apple-Silicon only), sandboxd (egress default-allow; ruleset is unshipped roadmap). FALLBACK: CubeSandbox (78 contributors, ships vmlinux offline) but it needs MySQL+Redis+containerd and almost certainly exceeds the whole OI-4 budget alone. GATE: WD-12. BLOCKER: measure matchlock+kernel footprint against the 150MB cap BEFORE committing.
Target: DEFERRED - unscheduled (own ADR + WD-12); re-enters on merit. CEO 2026-08-19

Title: Governed harness integration - layer 2
Description: Make the governance plane the runtime that existing agent harnesses plug into, WITHOUT forking any of them. Strategy ratified 2026-08-10: 40+ harnesses exist and churn quarterly, so forking one picks a loser; the durable positions are MCP-as-tool-protocol, the approval moment and the evidence trail, all three of which we already own. Reference integrations (both expose block-and-wait as a first-class REMOTE protocol, so integration is a client not a patch): OpenHands agent server - POST /confirmation_policy, POST /security_analyzer, POST /respond_to_confirmation (NOTE the OpenHands/OpenHands repo has PIVOTED to an Electron control center; the agent now lives in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk, MIT); and openworker - GET /v1/inbox plus POST /v1/inbox/{id}/resolve, MIT, whose permissions.py is worth reading as prior art (it rejects any command containing shell operators BEFORE prefix-matching argv, precisely because 'git status' would otherwise auto-approve 'git status && rm -rf ~'). openworker RISK: 14k stars against 130 commits / 8 contributors / 3 weeks old, plus two default-on cloud egress paths (an AWS API-Gateway WSS relay and telemetry) that must be disabled for air-gap. DEPENDS ON B-040 - a harness that is not contained would have to choose to call us. STUDY BUT DO NOT ADOPT: nearai/ironclaw, a competing governance plane whose InvocationFingerprint (SHA-256 over canonicalized scope/capability/estimate/input) is the same anti-swap property as ours, but whose seams are Rust traits in a composition root, so adoption means a fork of an 884-crate tree.
Target: v1.0.0 (own ADR + WD-13); ships as COOPERATIVE governance while B-040 is deferred - limitation must be stated in the v1.0.0 criteria

Title: Audit-chain external verifiability
Description: Our chained-hash audit is unkeyed SHA-256 computed and stored by audit-service itself, so it proves ORDERING but not AUTHENTICITY: an attacker who achieves write access to the audit store - precisely the RCE-on-api scenario SEC-20 took seriously - can recompute the entire chain from genesis and the result verifies clean. There is no signature over chain heads with a key the writing service does not hold, no periodic witness or notarization, and no append-only enforcement below the application. OWASP ASI08 (Repudiation and Untraceability). PRIOR ART: Agent-Field/agentfield signs with Ed25519 into W3C VC bundles that a third-party auditor verifies OFFLINE with bundled DIDs, without database access or trust in the control plane - strictly ahead of us; microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit both chains AND HMACs each entry (symmetric, so it shares our key-compromise weakness). Given a chained-hash audit is listed as a DIFFERENTIATING control, 'our chain is only as trustworthy as the service that writes it' is the finding most likely to land hardest in the v1.0 security capstone. Scoped into v1.0 as E-06/S-28 because it hardens an existing control and adds no governed mutation.

Title: Bundle provenance - signing and SBOM
Description: For an air-gapped product the offline bundle IS the trust root, and our release gates are functional (task offline-bundle, size and version checks) rather than provenance: no bundle signature, no SBOM. An operator installing on a disconnected network has no cryptographic way to confirm the bundle is the one we built. OWASP ASI04 (Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities) - a full category against which we currently map no control at all. PRIOR ART: agent-governance-toolkit ships SBOM generation and diffing, ClusterFuzzLite, CodeQL and gitleaks; even toolport at 146 stars does tool rug-pull detection and quarantine. Release engineering, not product capability, so it passes the v1.0 boundary rule. SECOND FRONT (deferred): tool-side attestation for the TR-2 external-MCP proxying work, which walks straight into ASI04 with no manifest pinning designed.
